cards.text: This is a psalm of David, a song for the dedication of the temple, and David's talking straight to the LORD. He opens with, "I will exalt You, O LORD," because the LORD lifted him up. Friend, NOBODY appreciates getting lifted up like a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD lifted David up. What does David say the LORD didn't let his foes do?

cards.text: Then David tells how it went down. Not a polite little text, friend, he CRIED to the LORD for help.

cards.question: David cried to the LORD for help, and the LORD ___ him.

cards.text: And this was no paper cut, friend. David says the LORD pulled him up from Sheol and spared him from going down into the Pit.

cards.question: True or false: By Sheol and the Pit, David means he came close to dying.

cards.text: Then David turns to everybody else and calls them in: "Sing to the LORD, O you His saints, and praise His holy name." He went from crying for help to LEADING THE CHOIR.

cards.question: David gives the LORD's saints a reason to sing. What does he say about the LORD's anger?

answers.text: It's fleeting next to His favor
It falls only on His foes

cards.question: David has another line for the saints: weeping may stay the night. True or false: he says joy comes in the morning.

cards.text: Now David gets honest about himself. There was a time he said, "I will never be shaken."

cards.question: David once said, "I will never be shaken." When does he say he talked like that?

cards.text: Back then, the LORD had favored him and made his mountain stand strong. I felt that solid on my old kitchen counter too, right up until a SHINY new stamper showed up.

cards.question: Then everything changes for David. The LORD ___ His face, and David was ___.

cards.text: So David calls to the LORD and begs for mercy. Then he makes his case like it's closing arguments.

cards.question: David asks the LORD, "Will the dust praise You?" What's his point?

answers.text: If he dies he can't praise the LORD
Even dust will praise the LORD someday
His foes are worth no more than dust

cards.text: Then David boils it all down: hear me, have mercy, be my helper. No fancy speech this time, friend. Just HELP.
And David says the LORD turned his mourning into DANCING. When joy hits me, I'm hopping around on this gold base like the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: The LORD peeled off David's sackcloth and clothed him with ___.
Why does David say the LORD clothed him with joy?

answers.text: So his heart would sing and not be silent
So his foes would see it and be ashamed
So the people would follow him to battle

cards.question: David closes with a promise to the LORD. True or false: he says he'll give thanks until his troubles are over.

findings.problem: David appears for the first time and is never introduced. The card names him without saying who he is, such as David, king of Israel.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 1 already says the LORD lifted David up, so the wrong answers "ignored" and "scolded" are ruled out before the baker reaches this card. The real choice is a single option, and the two wrong answers aren't believable.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says this line is David's reason for the saints to sing. That setup rules out the wrong answer "It outlasts His favor", because it can't be a reason to sing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card gives the first half of Psalm 30:5b, "weeping may stay the night", then asks whether the line goes on "joy comes in the morning." That asks the baker to confirm the next words of the line, not its meaning or movement.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question opens with "Then everything changes for David", and card 12 just said David was favored and his mountain stood strong. Together they rule out "lifted" and "thrilled", which leaves only the right pair.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Then David boils it all down...", "No fancy speech this time, friend." and "Just HELP."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke "When joy hits me..." puts the word "joy" right before card 18, which asks the baker to fill in that the LORD clothed David with ___ (joy). This gives the answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
